senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: the arm bent as in a position to receive or hold something
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is not necessary to speak of ‘bent arms’ in translating Luke 2:28, since the context itself indicates the presumed position of the arms.

senses.def: a person in the genealogy of Jesus (Matthew 1:13)
any kind of plant with sharp projections on its stem and/or branches; regarded as useless; symbol of hardship
senses.comment: Since plants having thorny projections are almost worldwide in distribution, there is no difficulty in obtaining a satisfactory term for such plants. In some instances, however, a descriptive equivalent may be necessary, for example, ‘plants with piercing points’ or ‘plants that stick into one’s flesh.’

senses.def: (a borrowing from Hebrew, literally: praise Yahweh) an expression of praise
a generic term for any kind of spice, though often a specific reference to amomum, an Indian type of spice
senses.comment: In most translations ἄμωμον is interpreted as spice in general, and though in all languages some types of herb-derivative condiments are employed, there may be no general term for such spices. One may, however, in some instances use a descriptive phrase, for example, ‘good-tasting herbs’ or ‘flavoring leaves.’

senses.def: to remain in a place and/or state, with expectancy concerning a future event
to move up
senses.comment: The upward movement may be of almost any gradient, for example, in going up a road to Jerusalem (Galatians 1:17) or in going up into a tree (Luke 19:4) or in ascending into heaven (Acts 2:34).

senses.def: (derivative of Ἀντιόχεια ‘Antioch,’ 93.405) a person who lives in or is a native of Antioch
serious and strong criticism based upon presumed evidence
a city in Macedonia
(derivative of ῥάπτω ‘to sew together,’ not occurring in the NT) pertaining to being without a seam, that is, without being sewn together
senses.comment: In some languages it may be necessary to describe such a seamless robe as ‘his robe was woven as just one piece of cloth.’

senses.def: a Christian in Colossae

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (derivative of ἀτακτέω ‘to do nothing,’ 88.246) pertaining to refusing to work
senses.comment: For a discussion of ἀτακτέω in the related context of 2 Thessalonians 3:7, see 88.246.

senses.def: the state of not using one’s capacity for understanding
any kind of plant with sharp projections on its stem and/or branches; regarded as useless; symbol of hardship
senses.comment: The reference to the passage of Scripture in Luke 20:37 is supplied from the context.|Except for Luke 6:44, all occurrences of βάτος in the NT are to the burning bush of, in which the reference may very well be to a ‘burning thorn bush.’

senses.def: a Hebrew liquid measure of between eight and nine gallons or approximately thirty-five liters
senses.comment: Because of the possible symbolic numerical values used in the Parable of the Dishonest Steward, it is important to retain the numerals, while making some adjustment in the case of the term βάτος. Accordingly, one may speak of ‘one hundred barrels of olive oil’ or ‘one hundred containers of olive oil’ or ‘one hundred large jars of olive oil.’

senses.def: a person in the genealogy of Jesus
an alternative form of Βόες[a] (93.78)
biological or legal parents
a league of ten cities in a region east of the Jordan
to clean out or to clean off thoroughly
to succeed in fleeing from
to cause people to rebel against or to reject authority
the area on the top of a flat-roof house
senses.comment: The phrase κηρύξατε ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων ‘proclaim from the housetops’ (Matthew 10:27) is an idiom meaning ‘to proclaim publicly’ (see 28.64). See 7.50 for comments relating to translational problems.

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: on the housetops) pertaining to being widely known in view of the events in question having taken place in public
the meat of animals which have been sacrificed to idols
glosses: meat of animals sacrificed to an idol
senses.comment: εἰδωλόθυτον is a semantically complex word meaning literally ‘that which has been sacrificed to idols.’ There is no specific element meaning ‘meat,’ but the stem meaning ‘sacrifice’ implies ‘meat.’ Part of the sacrifice was normally burned on the altar, part was eaten during a ritual meal in a temple, and part was sold in the public market. According to Jewish tradition this meat was unclean and therefore forbidden. εἰδωλόθυτον is normally translated by a phrase, for example, ‘meat which had been offered to idols’ or ‘meat of an animal which had been sacrificed to idols’ or ‘meat of animals killed in honor of false gods.’

senses.def: to form ideas which are unrelated to reality, normally with a negative connotation
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand ἐκζήτησις in 1 Timothy 1:4 as meaning ‘controversies’ or ‘arguments’ (see 33.442).

senses.def: a dispute involving empty speculation
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἐκζήτησις in 1 Timothy 1:4, see 31.33.

senses.def: pertaining to being extremely afraid

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to be so furiously angry with someone as to be almost out of one’s mind
senses.comment: In some instances it may be possible to render ἐμμαίνομαι in Acts 26:11 as ‘to be so angry as to be like an insane person.’

senses.def: (derivative of ἐνεργέω[a] ‘to function, to work,’ 42.3) that which is done, with possible focus on the energy or effort involved
to be in extreme despair, implying both anxiety and fear
a position above another, whether or not in contact
a degree which is significantly in excess of some amount

senses.subdomain: High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
senses.def: a marker of superior status, suggesting an additional factor of degree
senses.comment: See discussion at 84.13.

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: pertaining to the philosophical system of the Greek philosopher Epicurus, who taught that the world is a series of fortuitous combinations of atoms and that the highest good is pleasure
senses.comment: In most instances translators have found it more satisfactory to simply transliterate the terms Ἐπικούρειος and Στοϊκός (11.97), but some supplementary note to identify the teachings of the Epicureans and Stoics is important.

senses.def: to express strong disapproval of someone
to command, with the implication of a threat
extension from a source which is inside
the inner surface of an object
(a figurative extension of meaning of ἔσωθεν[a] ‘from inside,’ 84.14) the inner being of a person as the source or agent of thought or behavior
senses.comment: A literal translation of ἔσωθεν δέ εἰσιν λύκοι ἅρπαγες in Matthew 7:15 as ‘on the inside they are ravaging wolves’ could be seriously misleading, since in some cultures certain people are regarded as actually being animals but disguised as human beings. It may therefore be necessary to make some adjustments in this passage and to translate as ‘but what they want to do makes them like wild wolves’ or ‘but their minds are like the minds of wild wolves.’ On the other hand, one could employ a strictly literal translation and then have a footnote indicating that this statement in the Scriptures does not confirm local beliefs concerning animals disguised as humans.

senses.def: to be financially well off
senses.comment: It may be useful in some languages to translate εὐπορέομαι in Acts 11:29 as ‘each one was to do this in proportion as he had more than he needed’ or ‘… in proportion to the amount of possessions which he owned.’

senses.def: having a deep concern for or devotion to someone or something

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: a particularly strong feeling of resentment and jealousy against someone
a high point on a scale of extent and implying intensity of involvement
any type of sound, tone, or noise other than human speech
senses.comment: In a number of languages it will be essential to make a clear distinction between various types of sound referred to by ἦχος[a]. The sounds of a cymbal, a trumpet, and the sea are very frequently referred to by entirely different terms.

senses.def: information concerning a person or an event
any living creature, not including man
any four-footed animal, either wild or domesticated
senses.comment: A high percentage of languages appear to have no generic term to identify all kinds of quadrupeds whether wild or domesticated. Rather, they tend to make quite clear distinctions between wild and domesticated animals, and therefore it may be necessary to indicate both types in those contexts where the reference is to both wild as well as domesticated animals. For example, one may sometimes speak of ‘animals of the grass and animals of the forest’ or ‘animals of the barn and animals of the mountains.’|In Acts 10:12 the reference is primarily to wild animals, since for the most part wild animals would be those designated as unclean. However, swine were also regarded as unclean, and they were domesticated.|In Revelation 13:1ff two visionary creatures are referred to by the term θηρίον ‘beast.’ Despite their strange symbolic appearance, they would no doubt be included within the potential range of reference of θηρίον[b].

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of θηρίον[b] ‘(wild) animal,’ 4.4) a bad person, in the sense of being both harmful and dangerous
senses.comment: The translation of θηρίον[c] as merely ‘wild animal’ may be seriously misunderstood in some languages, since speaking of a person as ‘a wild animal’ might be a compliment based upon the idea of strength and courage. It may, therefore, be necessary to use some such expression as ‘dangerous animal’ or ‘harmful wild animal.’

senses.def: to serve as a priest in the performance of religious rites and duties
senses.comment: In contrast with the prophet who speaks to people on behalf of God, the priest is often defined as one who represents the people before God. In reality, however, the priest is one who is primarily engaged in religious ritual and ceremony in contrast with the prophet, whose primary activity is involved in proclaiming a message. In societies in which there is no organized priesthood and where there are only medicine men or shamans, it has often been possible to translate ἱερουργέω and ἱερατεύω as simply ‘to be God’s shaman.’ Whether such an expression can be used depends very largely upon the connotations associated with shamanism.

senses.def: a son of Jacob and ancestor of an Israelite tribe
a marker of coordinate relations
marker of a sequence of closely related events
a marker of an additive relation which is not coordinate
a marker of emphasis, involving surprise and unexpectedness
a marker of a new sentence, but often best left untranslated or reflected in the use of ‘and’ or the conjunctive adverb ‘then.’
a marker of a totality of two closely related elements
senses.comment: The double use of καί in Mark 9:13 may merely reflect a Semitic tendency.

senses.def: to hit or strike with sufficient impact so as to knock an object down
senses.comment: It is possible to interpret καταβάλλω in 2 Corinthians 4:9 as meaning ‘to hurt badly’ (see 20.21).

senses.def: to cause someone to suffer considerable pain or injury
senses.comment: It is possible that in 2 Corinthians 4:9 καταβάλλω should be understood as ‘to knock down’ (see 19.10).

senses.def: to put or place something down, with the implication of permanence
a state of not being able to think satisfactorily because of complete bewilderment and stupor
to bring serious charges or accusations against someone, with the possible connotation of a legal or court context
(derivative of κηρύσσω[c] ‘to preach,’ 33.256) the content of what is preached
one who participates with another in some enterprise or matter of joint concern
the flesh of animals used as food
senses.comment: In some languages a distinction is made between the meat of wild animals and meat of domesticated animals. In Romans 14:21 and 1 Corinthians 8:13 it is the latter which is involved.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: drinking parties involving unrestrained indulgence in alcoholic beverages and accompanying immoral behavior
a bowl in which incense is burned
(derivative of Μαγδαλά[c], a woman of Magdala
to become useless and hence worthless
to effect a change of location in space, with the implication that the two locations are significantly different
glosses: to move from one place to another

senses.def: to change from one state to another
a Roman mile, consisting of a thousand paces and equivalent to somewhat less than an English mile but equal to about one kilometer and a half
senses.comment: In translating Matthew 5:41 in the metric system, it would be better to simply say ‘whoever forces you to carry his pack one kilometer’ rather than to attempt more specific distance, namely, ‘a kilometer and a half.’

senses.def: the condition resulting from being severely hurt or wounded
(derivative of Νικόλαος[a], 93.283) a follower of Nicolaus (1)
to be on a journey, presumably with the focus upon being en route
to speak with someone, with the implication of a reversal of roles in communication

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: pertaining to being early in the morning
pertaining to a benefit to be derived from some ob ject, event, or state
senses.comment: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘benefit’ or ‘beneficial’ is often ‘that which helps.’ Accordingly, in 1 Timothy 4:8 one may render ἡ γὰρ σωματικὴ γυμνασία πρὸς ὀλίγον ἐστὶν ὠφέλιμος as ‘physical exercise helps to a small extent’ or ‘if one exercises one’s body, that helps a little.’

senses.def: to announce what must be done
to be present at a particular time and place
to come to be present at a particular place
(derivative of πάρειμι[a], ‘to be present,’ 85.23) what one has on hand as available for use

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: a specific time corresponding to some other time
glosses: that which exists at any time

senses.def: (derivative of πείθω[a] ‘to persuade,’ 33.301) pertaining to being able to persuade or convince
to walk along or around
to live or behave in a customary manner, with possible focus upon continuity of action
(an idiom, literally: to walk in the tracks) to behave in the same manner as someone else
to come to believe something to be true
a population center, in contrast with a rural area or countryside and without specific reference to size

a population center of relatively greater importance (in contrast with κώμη[a] ‘village,’ 1.92, and κωμόπολις ‘town,’ 1.91), due to its size, economic significance, or political control over a surrounding area (it is possible that fortification of walls and gates also entered into the system of classification of a πόλις[b], in contrast with other terms for population centers)
senses.comment: Most languages spoken by people in urbanized and industrialized societies have a number of terms for different types of population centers, for example, metropolis, city, town, village, hamlet, etc. For so-called tribal languages the primary means for making gradations consists of added attributives, for example, ‘a very large village,’ ‘a large village,’ ‘a village,’ ‘a small village.’ A translator must simply attempt to be as consistent as possible in referring to different types of population centers mentioned in the Scriptures.

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: the inhabitants of a city

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: gentleness of attitude and behavior, in contrast with harshness in one’s dealings with others
senses.comment: In a number of languages ‘gentleness’ is often expressed as a negation of harshness, so that ‘gentleness’ may often by rendered as ‘not being harsh with people,’ but gentleness may also be expressed in some instances in an idiomatic manner, for example, ‘always speaking softly to’ or ‘not raising one’s voice.’

senses.subdomain: To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
senses.def: to plan ahead of time, with considerable thought and attention
to execute someone by nailing that person to a cross

senses.subdomain: Processes Involving the Mouth, Other Than Eating and Drinking
senses.def: to spit on or at something or someone
senses.comment: In some societies spitting has quite a different symbolic meaning than it has in the Western world. In fact, in some societies in Africa, to spit upon a person’s head is to confer a blessing. It may therefore be necessary in the case of Matthew 26:67 to translate ‘they spat in his face’ as ‘they spat in his face to dishonor him’ or ‘… to show their anger against him.’

senses.def: to become strengthened, with focus upon the source of such strength

senses.subdomain: Precious and Semiprecious Stones and Substances
senses.def: onyx, sardonyx, of varying colors (see 2.29)
an appropriate portion or ration of food (a type of food allowance)
glosses: a due amount of food rations
senses.comment: It is possible to interpret σιτομέτριον in Luke 12:42 as ‘the proper amount of food’ or ‘the food that was due them’ or ‘the food that should be given (to the servants).’ Since σιτομέτριον is a semantically complex term consisting of two quite distinct components, it is usually necessary to employ a phrase as a proper equivalent.

senses.def: to pull or drag, requiring force because of the inertia of the object being dragged
to live in conformity with some presumed standard or set of customs
senses.comment: In some languages it may be useful to restructure the relationships expressed by the reference to ‘the Spirit,’ and therefore one may translate this clause in Galatians 5:25 as ‘since the Spirit has given us life, we should also let him control our lives.’

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to follow in the tracks) to behave in the same manner as someone else
to bring false charges against someone, especially with the intent of personal profit
senses.comment: The term συκοφαντέω refers to a practice in which persons could bring charges against an individual and receive a part of the fine or indemnity paid to the court.

senses.def: to be associated with others in eating
a state of destruction and ruin
senses.comment: In some languages it is impossible to speak of ‘leaving ruin’ except in the sense of going off from ruin. Accordingly, it may be necessary to render this expression in Romans 3:16 as ‘they cause ruin and misery wherever they go.’

senses.def: pertaining to that which has been decided upon in advance
cardinal number, where there are four thousand instances of a countable entity
any kind of plant with sharp projections on its stem and/or branches; regarded as useless; symbol of hardship
senses.comment: Since plants having thorny projections are almost worldwide in distribution, there is no difficulty in obtaining a satisfactory term for such plants. In some instances, however, a descriptive equivalent may be necessary, for example, ‘plants with piercing points’ or ‘plants that stick into one’s flesh.’

senses.def: a dense growth of trees covering a relatively large area
senses.comment: In James 3:5 it is also possible to interpret ὕλη as wood which has been cut up, either firewood or wood used for construction (see ὕλη[b] wood, pile of wood, 3.64).|In some languages spoken by people living in tropical forest areas the equivalent of ‘forest’ is simply the expression ‘where no one lives,’ based upon the fact that people live in clearings and everything else is forest. Such a rendering, however, may not lead to a satisfactory translation of James 3:5 (the only occurrence of ὕλη in the NT), in which case one is better advised to interpret ὕλη in the sense of ‘pile of wood’ (3.64).

senses.def: the woody part of trees or bushes
senses.comment: In James 3:5 ὕλη may be interpreted as a forest (see 3.3).|As already noted in the case of ξύλον[a] (3.60), a number of languages make a distinction between wood used as building material and wood employed in heating or cooking.

senses.def: to cause to ascend
to respond to what has been said (in the NT restricted to responses to questions)
to assist in supplying what may be needed
to regard something as presumably true, but without particular certainty
senses.comment: In some languages the equivalent of ‘to suppose’ or ‘to presume’ is ‘to think somewhat’ or ‘to think perhaps’ or ‘to think a little.’ In some instances the lack of certainty is spelled out clearly as ‘to think, but not with certainty’ or ‘to think, but not to know’ or ‘to think, but not to be sure.’

senses.def: a box or crib where animals feed (or possibly even an open feeding place under the sky)
senses.comment: φάτνη[a] occurs only in Luke 2:7, and it may be important in some languages to distinguish clearly between various alternatives. The term ‘crib’ normally refers to the place where an animal stands when it feeds. The ‘manger’ is a relatively large box or rack containing hay, and a ‘feed box’ is a much smaller container, usually for grain. There is, of course, no way of knowing precisely where the baby Jesus was placed, but it would be very appropriate for the baby to have been placed in the feed box or in the manger. See also 7.64.

senses.def: a stall where animals are fed
senses.comment: φάτνη[b] may designate a part of a barn, or it may simply refer to a customary place where an animal is fed outside, often in a semi-enclosure (see 6.137).

senses.def: a deaconess of the church commended in Romans 16:1

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of χαλιναγωγέω ‘to control with bit or bridle,’ not occurring in the NT) to exercise close control over some function
senses.comment: In some languages the expression μὴ χαλιναγωγῶν γλῶσσαν αὐτοῦ in James 1:26 may be rendered as ‘one who does not tell his tongue what to say’ or ‘one who cannot tie his tongue down’ or ‘one who cannot stop his talking.’

senses.def: to lack something which is necessary and particularly needed
a marker of direct address (functionally equivalent to the traditional vocative)
senses.comment: Often left untranslated.
